title: Colour, and what light really is
scope: Use your school’s topic list to select the ideas you need. These are original practice questions with illustrative values and suggested self-marking guidance, not official Cambridge papers.

objectives.label: Explain how a prism separates white light into a spectrum.
objectives.note: Relate different refraction to wavelength; distinguish separating existing wavelengths from creating new colours.

objectives.label: Predict object and filter colours under specified illumination.
objectives.note: Track which wavelengths are available, reflected, transmitted or absorbed; distinguish additive light from pigment mixing.

objectives.label: Explain a blue sky and a redder direct Sun near the horizon.
objectives.note: Distinguish redirected scattered light from the direct beam and account for wavelength dependence and atmospheric path length.

objectives.label: Explain how absorption, path length and suspended material affect water colour.
objectives.note: Compare shallow and deep paths; control background and illumination and recognise limits of a coloured-water model.

objectives.label: Use light-wave relationships and polarisation evidence.
objectives.note: Calculate frequency from wavelength, compare electromagnetic waves in vacuum, and explain crossed polarising filters.

objectives.label: Account for energy and wavelength changes in Raman scattering.
objectives.note: Track energy exchange between a photon and material; distinguish ordinary elastic scattering from a characteristic Raman shift.

cards.definition: Different wavelengths can refract by different amounts in a material.
cards.explanation: Different wavelengths can refract by different amounts in a material. A prism separates existing colours rather than manufacturing them.
cards.example: White light can spread into a spectrum through a glass prism.
cards.confusion: A prism separates existing colours rather than manufacturing them.
cards.question: Explain dispersion and distinguish it from a common mistaken idea.
cards.answer: Different wavelengths can refract by different amounts in a material. A prism separates existing colours rather than manufacturing them.
cards.cue: A prism separates existing colours rather than manufacturing them.

cards.definition: The colour seen from an object depends on the illuminating spectrum and the light reaching the observer.
cards.explanation: The colour seen from an object depends on the illuminating spectrum and the light reaching the observer. A surface cannot reflect a wavelength absent from the illumination.
cards.example: An ideal red surface can look dark under blue-only illumination.
cards.confusion: A surface cannot reflect a wavelength absent from the illumination.
cards.question: Explain object colour and distinguish it from a common mistaken idea.
cards.answer: The colour seen from an object depends on the illuminating spectrum and the light reaching the observer. A surface cannot reflect a wavelength absent from the illumination.
cards.cue: A surface cannot reflect a wavelength absent from the illumination.

cards.definition: Small particles and molecules scatter different wavelengths by different amounts.
cards.explanation: Small particles and molecules scatter different wavelengths by different amounts. The daytime blue sky is not mainly a reflection of the sea.
cards.example: Shorter visible wavelengths scatter strongly in clear air.
cards.confusion: The daytime blue sky is not mainly a reflection of the sea.
cards.question: Explain scattering in the sky and distinguish it from a common mistaken idea.
cards.answer: Small particles and molecules scatter different wavelengths by different amounts. The daytime blue sky is not mainly a reflection of the sea.
cards.cue: The daytime blue sky is not mainly a reflection of the sea.

cards.definition: The colour of water depends on absorption, scattering, depth, contents and reflected surroundings.
cards.explanation: The colour of water depends on absorption, scattering, depth, contents and reflected surroundings. Every blue sea is not explained by sky reflection alone.
cards.example: Deep clean water preferentially absorbs longer visible wavelengths along a long path.
cards.confusion: Every blue sea is not explained by sky reflection alone.
cards.question: Explain water colour and distinguish it from a common mistaken idea.
cards.answer: The colour of water depends on absorption, scattering, depth, contents and reflected surroundings. Every blue sea is not explained by sky reflection alone.
cards.cue: Every blue sea is not explained by sky reflection alone.

cards.definition: Light is a transverse electromagnetic wave; polarisation concerns its transverse field orientation.
cards.explanation: Light is a transverse electromagnetic wave; polarisation concerns its transverse field orientation. Light does not need air as a travelling medium.
cards.example: Crossed ideal polarising filters can greatly reduce transmitted light.
cards.confusion: Light does not need air as a travelling medium.
cards.question: Explain light waves and polarisation and distinguish it from a common mistaken idea.
cards.answer: Light is a transverse electromagnetic wave; polarisation concerns its transverse field orientation. Light does not need air as a travelling medium.
cards.cue: Light does not need air as a travelling medium.

cards.definition: Inelastic scattering changes a photon’s energy while the material exchanges energy with it.
cards.explanation: Inelastic scattering changes a photon’s energy while the material exchanges energy with it. A changed colour is not automatically the same process as ordinary elastic scattering.
cards.example: A scattered photon can lose energy to a molecular vibration.
cards.confusion: A changed colour is not automatically the same process as ordinary elastic scattering.
cards.question: Explain raman scattering and distinguish it from a common mistaken idea.
cards.answer: Inelastic scattering changes a photon’s energy while the material exchanges energy with it. A changed colour is not automatically the same process as ordinary elastic scattering.
cards.cue: A changed colour is not automatically the same process as ordinary elastic scattering.
